facts.text: A honey bee hive is a busy home where many bees live together as one colony.
Honey bees build nests with wax cells and store honey inside them.
Honey bees are social insects, which means they need the colony to live and work.
Many honey bee colonies like to nest in enclosed spaces, such as hollow trees or beekeeper hives.
A honey bee colony has three kinds of adult bees: a queen, workers, and drones.
The queen is usually the mother of the bees in the hive.
There is normally one adult queen in a honey bee hive.
Worker bees are female bees, and they do most of the jobs in the hive.
Drones are male honey bees.
Drones have very large eyes and do not collect nectar or pollen.
Honeycomb is made of many little wax cells.
Honeycomb cells often have six sides, making a hexagon shape.
Worker bees make beeswax from wax glands on their bodies.
Worker bees use beeswax to build cells for honey, pollen, eggs, larvae, and pupae.
Bees warm and shape wax with their bodies, antennae, legs, and mouthparts as they build comb.
Worker bees fly to flowers to collect nectar and pollen.
Nectar is a sugary liquid made by flowers.
A honey bee uses its long tongue, called a proboscis, to lap up nectar from flowers.
Worker bees carry pollen in pollen baskets on their back legs.
Pollen can rub from a bee onto another flower, helping flowers make seeds.
Bees make honey from nectar.
A foraging bee carries nectar back to the hive in a honey stomach, also called a honey crop.
Inside the hive, worker bees pass nectar to other bees and help turn it into honey.
Worker bees fan their wings to help dry watery nectar into thick honey.
When honey is ready, bees seal the honeycomb cell with a wax cap.
Honey is food that helps the colony live when flowers are hard to find.
Honeycomb cells can hold eggs, larvae, and pupae as baby bees grow.
Worker bees care for the queen's young bees.
A worker honey bee begins as an egg and grows through larva and pupa stages before becoming an adult.
Worker bees feed young larvae inside the hive.
A larva that will become a queen is fed special food called royal jelly.
Young worker bees often clean cells, feed young bees, and tend the queen inside the hive.
Older worker bees often guard the hive, remove dead bees, and forage outside.
Worker bees can fan air through the hive to help cool and ventilate it.
Worker bees can cluster and vibrate their wing muscles to help warm the brood area.
A successful forager can do a waggle dance that tells other bees about the direction and distance to food.
A honey bee colony can work like one big living team, with each bee doing part of the work.
